task: Repair two Mistral Python client OpenTelemetry tests whose implicit event-loop lifecycle fails on Python 3.14

subtasks.description: Discover and freeze a public CI or test-infrastructure failure without disturbing existing AEG work
lessons: An open issue can be stale even when it reports exact failing tests; verify that the frozen commit still contains the failing state before dependency setup.
When the default branch is already fixed, a reported affected release can provide objective historical replay evidence, but it must be classified as non-blind if the fix was already observed.

subtasks.description: Query the verified AEG library before solving and preserve below-threshold evidence
lessons: The best verified record scored 0.0373 against a 0.05 threshold and concerned repair-lab telemetry, so abstention was more useful than injecting generic repair context.
Run a zero-threshold diagnostic only to audit abstention; do not reinterpret below-threshold records as recommendations.

subtasks.description: Reproduce the two event-loop failures on the issue-reported v2.3.2 release under Python 3.14
lessons: Use the exact named node IDs and runtime version so a removed ambient runtime behavior is distinguished from unrelated suite failures.

subtasks.description: Replace obsolete implicit event-loop acquisition with an explicit lifecycle at two test call sites
lessons: For synchronous tests that execute one coroutine, asyncio.run provides an explicit create-run-close lifecycle and remains compatible with older supported Python versions.
Keep the repair in test infrastructure when product behavior is already correct; do not add a runtime compatibility shim to production code.

subtasks.description: Verify focused tests, the containing module, full suite, and one-file lint and format checks
lessons: Install declared optional extras when broad collection fails on an optional integration, then rerun rather than misclassifying the collection error as a patch regression.
Preserve skipped external-integration tests and future-runtime deprecation warnings as limitations even when the relevant suite is green.

constraints: Use only public Apache-2.0 source and public issue metadata.
Do not access credentials, paid services, private data, or proprietary repositories.
Do not push, comment, open a pull request, or trigger upstream workflows.
Keep external-project changes separate from existing AEG branches and working trees.
Do not claim independent diagnosis or causal AEG benefit because the historical repair was non-blind.
lessons: Verify issue freshness at the exact frozen commit before installing dependencies; stale reports otherwise consume the pilot budget without a reproducible pre-fix state.
For Python runtime removals, replay on the reported affected release and exact new runtime gives a strong before/after oracle.
AEG correctly abstained because its verified library had no asyncio or Python runtime-upgrade experience; generic verification overlap remained below threshold.
A successful historical replay is repair evidence, not evidence of upstream need, maintainer acceptance, independent patch discovery, or causal retrieval benefit.

metrics.interpretation: Three bounded candidate attempts produced one objectively verified historical repair. No controlled baseline-versus-assisted model comparison was run, so no causal AEG improvement is claimed.

limitations: Blindness was not preserved: the issue body disclosed the suggested edit, and the default branch's already-fixed call sites were observed before the historical manifest was frozen.
The repair targets historical v2.3.2; current main already contains equivalent asyncio.run usage, so there is no remaining upstream code change to contribute.
GitHub Actions logs were not retrieved because local gh authentication was expired; objective local reproduction replaced log-based claims.
The full suite skips 46 tests that require external Azure or GCP services.
pytest-asyncio 0.23.8 emits 11523 Python 3.16 deprecation warnings during the full Python 3.14 suite; these are separate from issue #490.
The schema requires a publication.pullRequest URL even for an unpromoted local candidate; this record uses the source issue URL and discloses that no PR exists.
Upstream maintainer acceptance is absent and distinct from local verification.
